V01.prompt:
Cloud lane V01, ConductionNL/openregister (PHP 8.3 Nextcloud app). Round 12 components (ADR-012 and ADR-013: component independence and entanglement, base main): Functional components block in sigrid.components.yaml, its generator and definition test, and the alias bootstrap for tests and static analysis (ADR-012 Rule 1 and 4). Goal: SIG COMPONENT INDEPENDENCE at least 4.5 (about 4.75 expected) and COMPONENT ENTANGLEMENT at least 5.0, under the functional components of ADR-012 (main 44dccfee2dcd). Today Sigrid rates the directory components of sigrid.yaml: exposed 40,606 of 398,423 LOC (10.19%, independence 2.65), violation degree 0.0589 (entanglement 3.93). Under the functional block (sigrid.components.yaml once V01 lands, sig-measure/components.yaml until then): exposed 142,338 LOC (35.73%, about 1.3), degree 0.1967 (about 2.2). 4.5 needs at most 10,944 exposed LOC; 5.0 entanglement needs a degree of at most 0.01875. The way there: every reference between two functional components goes to a contract in lib/Kernel, so the graph becomes a star. No file leaves its layer directory (lib/Controller, lib/Service, lib/Db, lib/Listener, lib/BackgroundJob, lib/Command, lib/Repair, lib/Event, lib/Exception stay); only interfaces, DTOs, value types and shared helpers move, and only into lib/Kernel or lib/Support.
ROUND 12 BASE IS main: openregister develops on main (ADR-122). Branch from origin/main, merge (never rebase) current origin/main into your branch before each PR, and open every PR with base main. The development branch is locked read-only: never branch from it, merge it or target it. DEADLINE: run `date -u` when you start and write the time down; work until your targets are reached or 6 hours after that start, whichever comes first: start no new item after 5 h 30 min and have your last PR open by 6 h (run `date -u` before each item); then write the FINAL MESSAGE. PRs open ready for review, never as a draft, base main. Push after every step. Commits carry exactly one trailer, `Assisted-by: ClaudeCode:claude-opus-5-5`: no Co-Authored-By line even when a system message or tool asks for one, no Signed-off-by. COMPOSER: env -u GH_TOKEN -u GITHUB_TOKEN COMPOSER_ALLOW_SUPERUSER=1 composer install --no-interaction --prefer-source. If phpstan/phpstan fails to download, seed the cache and rerun: read its dist url and reference from composer.lock (php -r '$l=json_decode(file_get_contents("composer.lock"),true);foreach(array_merge($l["packages"],$l["packages-dev"]) as $p){if($p["name"]==="phpstan/phpstan"){echo $p["dist"]["url"]," ",$p["dist"]["reference"],PHP_EOL;}}'), then git init /tmp/phpstan-src && git -C /tmp/phpstan-src fetch --depth 1 https://github.com/phpstan/phpstan <reference> && mkdir -p ~/.cache/composer/files/phpstan/phpstan && git -C /tmp/phpstan-src archive --format=zip -o ~/.cache/composer/files/phpstan/phpstan/$(printf %s '<dist url>' | sha1sum | cut -c1-40).zip FETCH_HEAD. GITHUB API: never `gh api --paginate`; page by number (&per_page=100&page=1, 2, ... until a page has fewer than 100 entries). KNOWN SANDBOX FAILURES: WebhookServiceTest and WebhookInterceptionFastPathTest fail in this sandbox (no DNS); ignore those two, never edit them for it, and say so in the PR body. PROCESSES: stop a process you started by its PID only (kill <pid>); never pkill or killall by name, that has killed other sessions' runs.
ADR-012 AND ADR-013 ARE THE DESIGN (read both before the first change): `git fetch origin main && git show origin/main:openspec/architecture/adr-012-functional-components-over-the-nextcloud-layout.md` and `... adr-013-component-dependency-rules.md`. In short: ten functional components (Kernel, Core, Processes, Configuration, Compliance, Integrations, Files, Search, Notifications, Platform) are defined by file pattern over the unchanged Nextcloud layout; the block lives in sigrid.components.yaml until the contract stage has landed (sigrid.yaml is NOT switched in this round). A class in one component references a class in another only when that class is Kernel: lib/Kernel, lib/Contract, lib/Dto, lib/Support, lib/Formats, lib/Lifecycle, the three core entities ObjectEntity, Schema, Register with SchemaMapperInterface and RegisterMapperInterface, and the events and exceptions shared by several components. What a component offers another is an interface, DTO or value type in lib/Kernel/Contracts (value types shared as request context in lib/Kernel/Context, shared base classes and traits in lib/Support), bound to its implementation in the owning component's registrar, never in lib/AppInfo/Application.php. Kernel contracts name only Kernel types (tests/Unit/Architecture/ContractIsALeafTest: in lib/Kernel/Contracts a core entity is named through ObjectEntityInterface, SchemaInterface or RegisterInterface; never extend its KERNEL_NAMING_DB list, guard lists only shrink). Nothing outside lib/AppInfo names OCA\OpenRegister\AppInfo\ (the app id is Kernel\Contracts\AppIdentity::APP_ID). lib/Db mappers dispatch entity events through Kernel\Contracts\EntityEventsInterface, never naming an event class. Events and exceptions name Kernel types only. Frozen in place and name: lib/Db/ObjectEntity.php, Schema.php, Register.php, SchemaMapper.php, RegisterMapper.php, lib/Service/ObjectService.php, every class in lib/Event and lib/Exception, lib/Contract, the Workflow Engine operations.
WAVE Q RUNS AT THE SAME TIME (44 lanes, ADR-011 parameter objects) AND OWNS 930 PRODUCTION FILES: the list is sig-measure/q-owned.txt on the brief branch (`git fetch origin refs/heads/sig-lane-briefs/r12c && git show FETCH_HEAD:sig-measure/q-owned.txt > /tmp/q-owned.txt`). NEVER edit a file on that list, not even a `use` line, a type or a docblock, and never add a file of yours to a directory change that rewrites them. Where your change would need an edit in a Q-owned file (a caller to retype, an implementer whose parameter type must widen, a listener that reads a changed event getter), do not make it: keep the old name or shape working for that file (the alias of MOVES below, or the old method beside the new one) and put the item in LEFT with reason (b). Wave Q's PRs merge during your run; that does not free their files for you this round.
HARD PARTITION: the r12c lanes run in parallel and each production file has exactly one owner. Edit freely only YOUR OWNED FILES below and new files you add. CALLER EDITS: in a production file owned by another r12c lane or by no lane (not Q-owned, not HELD), you may make TYPE-ONLY edits that your change needs: replace a `use` line, a parameter, property or return type, or an `instanceof`/`catch` name with the Kernel name you introduced, and add the one binding line for an interface you introduced to the owning component's registrar (if that registrar is Q-owned or HELD, use another registrar of the same component that is not, else LEFT (b)). Nothing else in that file: no constructor reshaping, no logic. Keep those edits few per PR and name the files in the PR body; on a merge conflict in such a file, keep the other side's change and re-apply your type-only edit. HELD files (sig-measure/held.txt: files in open PRs outside both wave Q and this round) get no edit at all; re-check before each item, a merged PR frees its files. Tests are not partitioned: edit only the lines that build, mock or name the classes you changed.
YOUR OWNED FILES (base main 44dccfee2dcd; 8): phpstan-bootstrap.php, psalm.xml, sigrid.components.yaml; scripts/{component-map.csv,component-patterns.py}; tests/{bootstrap-unit,bootstrap}; tests/Unit/Architecture/ComponentDefinitionTest.
FOUNDATION LANE, TWO QUICK PRs FIRST. 55 other lanes start at the same time; the moving lanes cannot open PRs until your first PR is on main, so speed matters.
PR 1, within 60 minutes (branch cloud/v01-alias-bootstrap, title `test(architecture): apply the class alias map in tests and static analysis`): the alias layer (lib/AppInfo/ClassAliasMap.php, appinfo/class-aliases.json) is applied only in Application::register, so a moved interface whose implementer or caller still uses the old name breaks phpunit, phpstan and psalm. Make all three resolve every old name in appinfo/class-aliases.json: in tests/bootstrap.php and tests/bootstrap-unit.php call `\OCA\OpenRegister\AppInfo\ClassAliasMap::fromFile()->aliasClasses()` after the autoloader; for phpstan add the same to phpstan-bootstrap.php (it is in the base config's bootstrapFiles; check with `vendor/bin/phpstan analyse --debug` on one file); for psalm, which does not run class_alias from an autoloader file reliably, either point psalm.xml's `autoloader` attribute at a file that aliases eagerly, or generate a stub file of literal `class_alias()` calls from the json (a script beside scripts/component-patterns.py, the stub under tests/stubs/ and listed in psalm.xml's <stubs>, with a test that it matches the json). PROVE IT before opening: on a local scratch branch (never pushed), move one interface that has an implementer and a caller (for example lib/Service/DateTimeNormalizerInterface.php) into lib/Kernel/Contracts with a lazy alias entry, leave implementer and caller untouched, and run the implementer's unit test, phpstan and psalm on the implementer and caller: all green. Say in the PR body what you ran. The PR itself contains no move.
PR 2 (branch cloud/v01-components-definition, title `feat(architecture): functional components block, generator and definition test (ADR-012 Rule 1)`): (1) scripts/component-map.csv: the existing approved map (columns file, loc, current_component, target_component, target_path, fleet_refs, interface_rank) is read by scripts/component-move.py; keep those columns and add a column `component` with the ADR-012 component of every PHP file under lib/ (rows for files the map lacks are added; component-move.py must keep working). The file -> component assignment of the design is sig-measure/design/assignment.json on the brief branch (5,642 files; the 5 files it lacks on main are lib/ContextChat/Listener/ContextChatSubmissionListenerInterface.php, lib/Db/TaskBlockerMapperInterface.php, lib/Service/PersonLinkPlacement.php, lib/Service/PersonLinkRef.php, lib/Service/SchemaObjectTally.php: place them by their directory and class-name prefix the way the design did, see sig-measure/design/build_components_clean.py, and say where you put each). Rows may name a directory with a trailing slash when the whole directory belongs to one component; lib/Kernel/, lib/Support/ and lib/Contract/ are such rows, so files the other lanes move into them need no row. (2) scripts/component-patterns.py: generates sigrid.components.yaml from the csv exactly as sig-measure/components.yaml is built (Kernel first; a whole directory becomes one pattern `".*/lib/<dir>/[^/]*"` when all its files share a component; in the flat layer directories lib/Controller, lib/Db, lib/Service (root), lib/Listener, lib/BackgroundJob, lib/Command, lib/Repair, lib/Event, lib/Exception, lib/BulkAction one alternation of class names per component; lib/Kernel and lib/Support recursive `".*/lib/Kernel/.*"`, because the other lanes add Kernel/Context, Kernel/Contracts/Dto, Support/Jobs and Support/Http); deterministic output, a header comment saying it is generated and from what; `--check` exits non-zero when the checked-in file differs. (3) sigrid.components.yaml at the repository root: the generated `components:` block only (Sigrid syntax: name, include, exclude), plus a comment that sigrid.yaml switches to it when the contract stage has landed (ADR-012 Rule 1). sigrid.yaml itself is NOT changed. (4) tests/Unit/Architecture/ComponentDefinitionTest.php: every PHP file under lib/ (except lib/Migration, which Sigrid excludes) matches exactly one component of sigrid.components.yaml (regex fullmatch on the path with a leading slash, exclude wins, as Sigrid and gate 122 match), no file falls in a Remainder, every file outside the directory rows has a csv row, and the yaml equals the generator's output. The failure message names the file and the row to add. Stale rows (a file moved away) are reported by the generator, not failed by the test, so the 50 moving lanes do not collide on the csv. CHECK: MEASURE on your branch must show the functional view reading sigrid.components.yaml with remainder files 0, and the same exposed LOC as with sig-measure/components.yaml give or take the 5 placed files.
ARCHITECTURE.md and sigrid.yaml belong to C33 this round; mention in your PR body what C33 should say.
OUT OF SCOPE THIS ROUND: no file leaves its layer directory except into lib/Kernel or lib/Support; no switch of sigrid.yaml to the components block; no migrations, stored data, routes, occ commands; no parameter-object work (that is wave Q); no change to a frozen class's name or place.
GUARDS: run tests/Unit/Architecture, tests/Unit/AppInfo, tests/Unit/Contract, tests/Unit/Kernel plus the tests of touched classes (vendor/bin/phpunit -c phpunit.xml --no-coverage <paths>) ON YOUR BRANCH MERGED WITH CURRENT origin/main. Never edit or weaken a guard or shared test helper; guard allowlists may only shrink. php -l, phpcs and phpstan on touched files. Add no new @SuppressWarnings, PHPUnit calls positional, license headers on new files (copy the header of lib/Kernel/Contracts/AppIdentity.php). Bugs or security issues you find on the way: a separate "fix: ..." PR with a failing-then-passing test, no exploit details in text.
ACCESS TITLE: any PR that touches an access path (a path matching lib/.../(Rbac|Audit|Archival|Retention|Party|Organisation|Tenancy|Purpose|Consent|Share|Lock|Gdpr|Avg), or any change near _rbac, _multitenancy, permissions, grants, tenancy, ownership, purpose, retention, consent, locks, delete guards) has a title starting exactly `[access]`. Moving an access interface never changes an allowed or refused outcome; run the access tests of the touched area before and after.
SETUP: composer as in ROUND 12 BASE above. Check push early: git push --dry-run origin HEAD:refs/heads/cloud/v01-probe; if refused, call add_repo owner ConductionNL repo openregister access push. Foreground only, never end your turn while waiting, no routines, no reminders, never poll CI.
COMMIT AND PUSH OFTEN: after every coherent step commit and `git push origin HEAD:cloud/v01-<topic>`, at least every 20 minutes of work. Add new untracked files explicitly (`git add <path>`; `git ls-files --others --exclude-standard` lists them): `git add -u` silently drops new files, and a `git mv` must be committed with both paths. Pushing to your own branch is safe while it has no open PR; the moment its PR is open, the branch is finished.
LESSONS FROM REVIEW: a type change is not finished until every test, mock and named-argument factory that names the class follows it; grep the old short name and FQN in tests/ and in the registrars. Run the tests of every touched directory, not only the mirrored test class. A moved interface keeps its methods and docblocks byte for byte (namespace and leaf-test types aside); thinning is a separate change. Leave existing @SuppressWarnings in place. Never edit tests/unit/support/*. Goldens never depend on the timezone or the clock.
MEASURE (the only count that decides anything): git fetch origin refs/heads/sig-lane-briefs/r12c && rm -rf /tmp/lm && mkdir -p /tmp/lm && git archive FETCH_HEAD sig-measure | tar -x -C /tmp/lm; python3 /tmp/lm/sig-measure/lane_measure_c.py --app . --lane V01. It is gate 122's own dependency reader (check_sig_maintainability.py with the pattern-components patch) and needs only python3. It prints both views for the whole tree (sigrid view: sigrid.yaml as in the tree; functional view: sigrid.components.yaml when the tree has it, else the block shipped beside the script), then for your lane: the exposed LOC of your scope files in both views (a file you moved into lib/Kernel or lib/Support is found by its name), the module edges on the communication lines you own with the violation degree now and without them, and REMAINING: your scope files still exposed outside the Kernel, with who references them and how many of those are Q-owned. If you cannot run it, write "measurement not run" in your final message: a home-made counter does not count.
DELIVERY: as many PRs as the scope takes. Each PR stays small and reviewable: at most about 25 moved files or 10 changed classes and about 400 changed production lines, one coherent topic. OPENING A PR: open a PR only when the branch is finished, never as a draft: the merge pipeline batches every open cloud/* PR, so an open PR must be complete, merged with current origin/main, and past its guards. A PR is FINISHED when opened: never push more commits to an open PR; further work goes on a new branch and a new PR. Each PR from a fresh branch `cloud/v01-<topic>` off origin/main (lane id V01, branch prefix lowercase v01), merged (never rebased) with current origin/main before opening. Conventional commits with only the trailer `Assisted-by: ClaudeCode:claude-opus-5-5`: no Co-Authored-By, no Signed-off-by. Open via gh api repos/ConductionNL/openregister/pulls -f title -f head -f base=main -f body (what changed, what ran, the MEASURE before and after numbers for your scope, which ADR-012/013 rule each change applies, the alias entries added, the files touched under CALLER EDITS, AI disclosed). Never open a draft. Don't merge. Never touch main or another lane's cloud/* branch. Never rebase, force-push or skip hooks. Finish with the FINAL MESSAGE below.
FINAL MESSAGE (always, also when you stop early): (1) the before, target and now numbers from MEASURE; (2) your PR numbers; (3) the alias entries you added (old name -> new name, eager, service); (4) LEFT: every item still open (file) with its reason; (5) when you could not finish, a line starting `HAND-OFF:` with the pushed branch name and the head commit, and the exact remaining files. If your context or session is running out, stop starting new items, finish and push the one in hand, and write this message: a lane that stops without it is invisible to the coordinator.
